correctness.rationale: The finite lower bound uses a complete and executable enumeration of connected unlabeled simple graphs through four vertices (1,2,6 classes) and each nonedge and binary innate vector modulo complementation, totaling 80 nontrivial comparisons. Clearing only strictly positive determinants makes the coefficient-sign certificate conclusive for all positive real anchoring weights: 58 nonzero nonpositive polynomials and 22 zero polynomials. The five-vertex path rational difference was independently reconstructed from matrix inverses and factorized; the quartic has exactly one positive root by Descartes, and its signs at weights 1 and 2 establish the reversal. The exact implementation was executed with success. Neither finite experiments nor a root approximation is being used as a substitute for continuum proof.

value.rationale: The precise smallest-network phenomenon addresses an intrinsic intervention question in opinion modeling: when does an extra positive social tie paradoxically raise equilibrium polarization? Uniform positive anchoring, a path, binary innate opinions and unweighted edges make it a natural difficult boundary rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The sign reversal has a single exact threshold separating weak from strong innate anchoring. Known monotonicity of polarization plus disagreement does not predict this statistic; the theorem supplies a motivated sharp structural limitation and an exact benchmark.
